text: The report concludes that over 90% of AMR gene occurrences are variable or rare across strains and that within-species variation is structured by resistance islands, phylogeny, and ecological ecotypes.
quote: Over 90% of AMR gene occurrences are variable or rare across strains, yet this variation is not random — it is organized into tightly co-inherited resistance islands, tracks phylogenetic structure, and in some species segregates into distinct ecotypes associated with ecological niche.
heading: Biological Significance

text: The report detects 1,517 resistance islands in 54% of species, with mean phi = 0.827, supporting frequent co-inheritance of AMR genes as multi-gene modules.
quote: The resistance island finding (1,517 islands in 54% of species, mean phi = 0.827) demonstrates that AMR genes are frequently co-inherited as multi-gene modules.
heading: Biological Significance

text: The report interprets the predominance of multi-mechanism resistance islands (88%) as suggesting selection for co-maintenance of complementary resistance strategies.
quote: The predominance of multi-mechanism islands (88%) suggests that natural selection favors the co-maintenance of complementary resistance strategies — for example, combining efflux pumps with enzymatic inactivation provides defense at multiple stages of antibiotic action.
heading: Biological Significance

text: Non-core acquired AMR genes show stronger phylogenetic signal than core intrinsic AMR genes in the report.
quote: The most surprising finding is that non-core (acquired) AMR genes show stronger phylogenetic signal than core (intrinsic) genes.
heading: Biological Significance

text: The report proposes that acquired resistance genes become stably integrated and vertically inherited after lineage acquisition, likely through mobile genetic elements, creating clonal AMR lineages.
quote: Our data suggest an alternative model: once a lineage acquires resistance genes (likely via mobile genetic elements), they become stably integrated into the genome and are vertically inherited, creating clonal AMR lineages.
heading: Biological Significance

text: The report states that near-universal core AMR genes (>=95% prevalence by definition) have near-zero Jaccard distances and little variance, suppressing distance-based metrics such as Mantel r and partially explaining their lower phylogenetic signal independently of biology.
quote: Core AMR genes, being nearly universal (>=95% prevalence by definition), have near-zero Jaccard distances with little variance, which inherently suppresses distance-based correlation metrics like the Mantel r — a statistical artifact that partially explains the lower signal, independent of biology.
heading: Biological Significance

text: The report cites Sanchez-Buso et al. (2020) for pangenomic perspectives on AMR emergence and maintenance and the complexity introduced by strain-specific AMR mechanisms.
quote: The extensive within-species AMR variation aligns with Sanchez-Buso et al. (2020) who described pangenomic perspectives on AMR emergence and maintenance, noting that strain-specific AMR mechanisms make resistance tracking far more complex than single-genome analyses suggest.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report states that 51% of AMR genes are rare within any given species.
quote: Our finding that 51% of AMR genes are rare within any given species quantifies this complexity at unprecedented scale.

text: The report cites Partridge et al. 2018 for the role of transposons, integrons, and genomic islands in co-mobilizing resistance determinants.

heading: Literature Context

text: The report interprets high resistance-island phi coefficients (mean 0.827) as suggesting inheritance of intact mobile elements rather than random assembly.
quote: The high phi coefficients (mean 0.827) suggest these elements are inherited as intact units rather than being randomly assembled.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report cites Maier et al. (2025) as finding that AMR gene transfer is largely confined to closely related lineages and that genetic compatibility negatively influences cross-species AMR transfer.

(2025) found that genetic compatibility negatively influences cross-species AMR transfer, supporting our observation that once acquired, resistance elements are maintained clonally.

text: The report concludes that variable AMR repertoires, resistance islands, and phylogenetic signal are general features of bacterial AMR biology rather than features limited to well-studied clinical species.
